issue_context.title: Vite SSR crashes if import has "assert"
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Acorn parser crashes if import (static or dynamic) has options with `assert`.

I am trying to implement strict Node.js support for Vitest and users who don't run code using vite-node or Vite SSR, which requires me to process assertions even though the proposal was moved to stage 3 with a syntax change (`assert` -> `with`), it would still be nice to support current Node.js runtimes.

You can see that the same code works correctly when running `node test.mjs` in reproduction.

Just adding this module should be enough (presumably):
- https://www.npmjs.com/package/acorn-import-assertions

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/node-ehr84c?file=index.mjs,test.mjs,file.json

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
npm install
node index.mjs
```

### System Info

```shell
Stackblitz
```


### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

_No response_

@bluwy what are your thoughts on the matter?

While `assert` is sort-of deprecated now, I think I'm fine with this since:

1. We still support it
2. Rollup supports it
3. `with` isn't widely supported yet so there's no nice migration path

So sounds good to me 👍 If you'd like to workaround this at the meantime too, you should be able to inject the acorn plugin through `rollupOptions.acornInjectPlugins` ([source code](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/61e801d10da8d67f6886993e4a723014d3865a08/packages/vite/src/node/server/pluginContainer.ts#L616-L620)). `ssrTransform` shares the same acorn parser.

review_comments: Maybe `__vite_ssr_dynamic_import__ `  and `__vite_ssr_import__` should throw an error if the runtime load a non-json module for the case. What do you think cc @sheremet-va ?

vite now will parse the json file's schema in the runtime, I think we could add some assertion validations in the parsing phase:

1. only `json` assert type is allowed like https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#import-assertions said
2. module's filepath suffix must be `.json` when assert type is `json`

If you really want to support Node.js logic, there are more checks with assertion:

- https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/lib/internal/modules/esm/assert.js

> If you really want to support Node.js logic, there are more checks with assertion:
> 
> * https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/lib/internal/modules/esm/assert.js

IIUC, only `json` assert type is supported for now according to 

https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/56c3263049dd75527155418e8f7f3a2bc2709f17/lib/internal/modules/esm/assert.js#L19-L45

IMO, a simple approach is  that checking whether the import statement matches the pattern like `import xxx from '*.json'  assert { type: 'json' }` or ` import('*.json', { assert: { type: 'json' } })`.

Another approach is that we could directly pass assert type to nodejs builtin `import()`. It's more robust with more complicated implementation.

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/91a18c2f7da796ff8217417a4bf189ddda719895/packages/vite/src/node/utils.ts#L969-L971

I think it already errors if it's a non-json module because Vite will try to convert to json to a js file and fails. But nonetheless if it's an issue, I don't think it's worthing working more on it as import assertions is already deprecated.
